title: fix(app-shell): lint an object validation rule's condition at the draft gate
body:
Fixes #9497

## What changed

`clientValidation`'s draft gate lints the four sibling surfaces at `scope: 'record'` —
`visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` and a `formula` field's `expression` — and
linted nothing at all on an object validation rule's CEL predicate. This adds the fifth
check of that same kind.

The server's rule evaluator (`rule-validator.ts` in `objectstack`'s `@objectstack/objectql`)
binds a validation predicate's context as `{ record, previous }` and nothing else, and its
`checkPredicate` fail-CLOSES an unevaluable predicate — re-read on `objectstack` `main`, not
taken from the card's transcription. The spec's Zod checks only the SHAPE of the predicate
(`ExpressionInputSchema`), so a bare-shorthand `amount > 100` — rather than
`record.amount > 100` — was accepted by the draft gate and then rejected **every** write to
the object. Measured directly against the resolved `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0:
`ObjectSchema.safeParse` ACCEPTS a draft whose validation rule reads `amount > 100`, and
ACCEPTS one that does not even parse as CEL (`record.amount >`).

⛔ Not an editor change. objectui#8167 gave the inline `ConditionBuilder` mount
`scope="record"`, which closes the editor route only; the JSON source editor, package import
and AI authoring routes all reach this gate without passing through that editor.

### Slots linted

| slot | rule types | server checker |
|---|---|---|
| `condition` | `script`, `cross_field` | `checkPredicate` |
| `when` | `conditional` | `checkConditional` |
| `then` / `otherwise`, recursively | nested rules | `evaluateRule`, same context |

`format`, `state_machine` and `json_schema` carry no CEL and are untouched. `when` is in
scope because the spec spells a `conditional` rule's guard that way and the server
fail-closes on it with the same sentence it uses for `condition` (its log line says
"when-predicate"); the nested branches, because `checkConditional` dispatches the taken
branch back through the same evaluator with the same context — the Validations panel's
`conditional` skeleton seeds exactly that nesting, so linting only the top level would leave
that predicate unlinted.

⛔ No `slot` hint is passed to `lintCelPredicate`, deliberately: `celAuthoring`'s slot-routed
verdict comes from `@objectstack/lint`'s `fieldRuleRootIssue`, whose bound-root set is the
FIELD tier's (`record` / `previous` / `parent`), while a validation rule binds `record` /
`previous` only. Adopting it here would import a judgement derived for a different surface.

⛔ `ObjectValidationEngine.scopeFor` is not cited and not wired — it stays deprecated and
pinned unwired.

### On `conditionScope.ts`, which landed under me mid-branch

`origin/main` was merged before this PR opened, and it brought objectui#8167's ruled
`CONDITION_SCOPE_BY_METADATA_TYPE`. Two rows matter and the code comment writes down both:

- its `validation` row is `record`, derived from the same server reading this gate uses ⇒
  the gate and the schema-driven editor reach one verdict from one authority, not from each
  other. The table is deliberately **not** imported here: it answers which scope a condition
  WIDGET may claim, and its `ConditionScope` carries a third value, `none`, that a gate
  cannot act on;
- its `object` row is `none`, and ⛔ that is not the row that governs this check. A future
  reader greping for `object` must not read it as overruling `scope: 'record'` here — the
  rules linted are validation rules, whichever door opened the object draft.

## Evidence

Everything below was run at `9aa05bbb6`, the final commit on this branch.

**Pre-fix red, with both controls green on both sides.** The implementation file alone was
taken back to `origin/main` (the new pin file kept), the pin re-run, then restored from
`HEAD` and proved byte-identical.

```
HEAD blob for target:      d7ba23ed78f76c2a8337dc39201f3cde4e4d1f14
pre-mutation marker count:  2   ->  post-mutation marker count: 0
mutated blob:              39e9975e7004cabcb33fb7184dcc95953f11b0fd  (differs — landed on disk)
PRE_FIX_VITEST_EXIT=1
restored blob:             d7ba23ed78f76c2a8337dc39201f3cde4e4d1f14  (byte-identical to HEAD)
git diff HEAD:             empty
```

Pre-fix verdict — `Tests  7 failed | 6 passed (13)`. The card's own spelling failed exactly
as it should:

```
FAIL … > flags a bare-shorthand condition with the record.FIELD fix
AssertionError: expected true to be false
- Expected   false
+ Received   true          ← res.ok was TRUE on `amount > 100` before this change
```

The two required controls were among the **6 green pre-fix**, and are green post-fix too:

1. `is clean for the canonical record.FIELD spelling` — `record.amount > 100` passes on both
   sides, so what is measured is a closed gap and not a linter that rejects everything.
2. `leaves the sibling field-rule verdicts exactly where they were` — one draft asserts both
   halves of a sibling key's verdict: a bad `visibleWhen` still flags with the
   `record.FIELD` fix, a good one still does not. A reader can see a check was added, not
   the function moved.

Post-fix: `Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests  13 passed (13)`.

All assertions go through `validateMetadataDraft`'s own verdict — the gate — never through
a helper's return value.

**Sibling regression surface.** All nine `clientValidation.*` test files together:
`Test Files  9 passed (9) · Tests  156 passed (156)`.

**Build closure + type-check**, serialised through the shared lock:
`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build && pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`
→ `VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 197s · waited 40s`. The dependency closure was
built first, so the `.d.ts` files that verdict read are this tree's and not a stale `dist`.
`type-check` is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `--listFiles` confirms the
new pin file is in the second project's program — the assertions are compiled, not only run.

**Gates** (each exit code captured before any pipe):

| gate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `check:changeset-presence` | exit 0 — 1 changeset declared for 1 released package |
| `check:new-line-citations` | `0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0` |
| `check:control-bytes` | `OK (scanned 7888 tracked text file(s))` |
| `check:test-path-roots` | exit 0 |
| `check:changeset-claims` | exit 0, report-only — see below |
| `check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
| `check:vi-mock-specifiers` | exit 0 |
| `check:unreferenced-sources` | exit 0 |
| `check:governed-queue-guard --test` (this diff's paths) | `NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) checked` |
| `eslint` on both changed files | exit 0 |

`check:changeset-claims` is report-only and names two pending changesets that mention
`clientValidation.ts`, addressed to the seat whose diff might have falsified them. Read:
neither is. One describes `LOADERS.flow` resolving the whole draft, the other the removal of
the dead `theme:` entry from `LOADERS`; this diff touches neither `LOADERS` nor the `flow`
path.

⛔ Whole-repo runs (`pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`) are CI's and were not run locally.

## Clause-②

`no` — counted off this diff, with what it does and does not prove.

- `git diff origin/main...HEAD | grep -c '^+export'` prints **0**, and this diff adds no
  added line matching `export` at all. That proves only that the branch adds no new
  top-level export statement; it is not by itself the clause-② answer, because a widening
  can land on an already-exported symbol.
- The symbol added, `validateObjectValidationRules`, is **module-private** — not exported —
  and the only public function whose behaviour moves, `validateMetadataDraft`, has an
  unchanged signature.
- `clientValidation` is absent from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` (0 occurrences;
  25 `metadata-admin` leaf re-exports there, control: 84 lines beginning `export`).
- Direction: the change **refuses** expressions the gate previously accepted. It narrows the
  accept set, which is the opposite of clause ②'s subject.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, ⛔ not fixed here and ⛔ not filed by this seat (returned in the
structured report for the triage seat to dedupe and file):

- **`ObjectValidationsPanel`'s `conditional` skeleton writes a key the spec refuses.**
  `makeSkeleton('conditional', …)` seeds `condition: 'false'`, and the panel's condition
  editor reads and writes `rule.condition` for that rule type — but the spec's
  `ConditionalValidationSchema` spells the guard `when` and rejects `condition` by name with
  `unrecognized_keys` ("Did you mean `condition` → `when`?"). Measured against the resolved
  `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0. The panel's own docblock promises every skeleton is "a VALID
  minimal skeleton … so the immediate object-draft save never 422s", so this is a
  reproducible contradiction of a stated contract, not a nit. Different defect class from
  this card — an editor writing the wrong key, versus a gate not linting — so it is not
  folded in here, and it is in a file this branch does not touch.
- Noted, not filed: the spec's `ConditionalValidation` docblock examples author `when` with
  bare-shorthand predicates (`account_type = "enterprise"`), the spelling the server
  fail-closes on. That is `objectstack`'s published documentation, reached by nothing in
  this repo's diff, and no pull request or person on this surface will carry it.
  Successor: none.

## Serial constraints

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/clientValidation.ts` is not among the four files
the second `domain:ui` seat's objectui#8167 claim names, and nothing here entered any of
them. `origin/main` was merged before this pull request was opened.
